complexity.notes: Uses division (prod // num), which the follow-up explicitly asks to avoid — the standard prefix/suffix product approach would be preferable. Slicing nums[:zero] and nums[zero+1:] creates unnecessary O(n) copies, and the match statement with a guarded first case is more verbose than simple if/elif. Correctness is fine given the constraints.
complexity.summary: Handles zeros as special cases: if there are multiple zeros the answer is all zeros; with one zero, only the zero position gets the product of the rest; otherwise it computes the total product and divides by each element.
